TLDR-TLDR: Humiliation Ritual: Master Cheap Collection

TLDR: The campaigns are mostly fine. Multiplayer lackluster. Entire menu system sucks majorly and is a blight compared to games from 25 years ago. The MCC is an insult to oldschool Bungie's passion, Halo 4 deserves to be KILLED in a back alley, I'm A CHUD, more news at 6

Disclaimer:
I can't really comment on the multiplayer because:
1.) I never play MP enough because even in the Halo 2 days I only ever got my ass handed to me and I'm not much of a MP person anyway. Most of my time was spent in local coop and splitscreen as well as Gearbox CE Multiplayer.
2.) The few times that I actually tried to get into a MP match on MCC, it was only after sitting in a queue for half an hour and setting the matchmaking filter to the equivalent of "just please god give me ANY lobby with more than 2 people in it"... So I stopped bothering and I haven't checked since.

The good:
So yeah that leaves me personally with just the campaigns to enjoy. And I do enjoy them, thoroughly (except 4). I appreciate that after all these years most of the bugs introduced in the Vista port of H2 and the Gearbox port of CE are finally ironed out. I appreciate that as mainly a PC gamer, I can play all the other Halo games from the comfort of my 1000W leaf blower. I f*cking also love the stuff that the Digsite team brought out.

However Ask yourself:
Should one be honestly be thankful about paying money to get a half baked product that got fixed ten years later? Should it take over a decade to fix a sloppy re-release of 5 old games +1 crap game? What exactly is the achievement here... Bungie handed them all the finished work on a platter. Microshaft, and 343i/Hole Studios had one job, and twiddled with their thumbs for a decade. So a large part of why this thing has good reviews now is not because this is or was a good product... it is because it rests entirely on the work of a studio from 25 years ago. Pat yourselves on the back everyone.

Bonus: "Halo" 4:
And honestly I couldn't give less of a sh*t about Halo 4 and anything afterwards if that wasn't apparent yet, in my opinion there was nothing worthy of the name Halo after Reach. Anything beyond is just like a bad fanfic, fight me in the comment section.

Let's get hateful:
My major gripe with this "Collection" is the way that this collection is collected. I should have seen it coming when I first started it up years ago; You start off being confronted with an annoying unskippable intro video from the companies that gave you nothing but pain. Thanks. Nothing new I guess but annoying nonetheless. Then you have to log in with a Microsoft account, which failed half the time due to some dumb error I couldn't care to elaborate. It's Games for Windows LIVE all over again!

...and then you get dropped into the main menu. Holy SH*T.

Flashback to some people at 343 probably, roughly 2013:
- Hey! Let's have Halo 4, the definitive game of the franchise, define the look of the MCC!
- Remember the epic, cinematic, monolithic 3D backdrops from the old Halo menus? Let's just... put some generic actionslop with a halo 4 skin there. How about a pile of bullets for example? When people think Halo, they think piles of brass and mortar shells like in CoD!
- Let's make the most horrible buttons that feel and sound like being shot at point blank with a cattle gun. We think this of our customers anyway.
- We actually need this whole beast to be impossible to navigate for anyone with any sense for a smooth UX, and the player needs to be pissed off before even getting to the Pillar of Autumn!
- Sane defaults? F*ck that. Let's make it almost mandatory to have to configure all settings, to get an even halfway playable experience.
- Oh yeah about that. I guess people are going to want 6 separate settings screens for each game by default!
#######

Settings woes:
You see... Chad Warden might look down on me for this, but I just wanted to play some Halo that day. Who could've known I had to wade through several pages of settings, just so I could get a control layout that I can handle without having to relearn everything I ever knew about vidya games, because whatever is the default is not what I remember from ANY previous Halo game. And you have to repeat this process for EVERY Halo game that you want to play. Sane defaults and / or cross game keyboard layouts. Why can't we have that? Am I just too dumb to see it in the UI? Then you have to repeat the same spiel for the graphics settings PER GAME. C'mon guys. I appreciate the granularity somewhat but wouldn't it have been better to make the settings somewhat cross-game as well, for those who just want to get going, and hide the per-game graphics settings behind some kind of advanced toggle? C'MON.

25 years ago...:
Have you BEEN in the main menu in OG Halo 1, 2 or 3? Were you not blinded by its majesty? Dumbstruck?
The animations were smooth and the sound design was pure s6x. The music made your spine rattle. The backdrops were stunning. The layout might've as well been done by Michael Okuda (look up LCARS). The immersion - PEAK. Those menus were simply the gateways to masterpieces.

Now LOOK at MCC. Clicking anything in this godforsaken menu feels like a stab in the ear and feels outright offensive to the senses. Everything is plastered with information. It is convoluted with duplicate buttons buttons buttons, (for example 2 separate ways to get to settings menu, 2 separate start buttons on the start mission screen for no reason, the list goes on) that to this day, some of the buttons I'm afraid to even click in fear of what might await me beyond. It is SOULLESS and distracting. 

Also, WHY is it, that when I load into a singleplayer game, I am confronted with thousands of options that honestly should be hidden by default, when most people just want to get into a normal game? How many buttons do I need to click to get into the damn game? Why does my mouse cursor need to travel the equivalent of my dad's way to school back an forth, just to launch a damn mission? WHY do I need a MP countdown timer before launching a SINGLEPLAYER mission??? Not to mention that the loading screens actively spoil parts of the story to new players (for example the flood intro is totally ruined in H1).

All these questions will never be answered. Just dust and echoes.

Here is my advice: Don't get this collection if you respect yourself, your money and OG Bungie's vision. There are better ways to enjoy the Bungie saga. Grab your old XBOX 360. Wait for emulators to get better. Wait for someone to vibecode a sourceport of the other games. Hell, play Halo CE, Gearbox edition with mods, or Halo 2 Vista with Project Cartographer. Anything but this sickly behemoth of corporate nostalgia milking.

343 Studios really screwed up the franchise/games. Online multiplayer matchmaking is abysmal and toxic af, "skill based" matchmaking means you're decent and then they just assume that you're good enough to go against "the pros" that haven't stopped playing in 15+ years at all times. No balance, no variation, no fun. 

They also have extreme optimization issues in terms of remastered maps, custom skins etc. There is no reason custom skins and remastering alone should cause crashes in the middle of matches unless you turn the custom skins off. And even then, it's a gamble that you'll make it through an entire match on 3 specifically. Then if their optimization issues cause a freeze and you have to exit the game, they penalize you for it with a temporary ban. 

You shouldn't be penalized for their lack of optimization causing your game to freeze. You shouldn't even be penalized for exiting a round if it really is the better move to make. Long story short, Bungie really screwed up handing over the franchise to 343 and really made a once beloved online multiplayer game nothing but an annoying pain in the ass now. Literally re-installed a few weeks ago and each time I play, I wonder why I still have it installed.

Being born in '99 means I was just a kid during the peak Halo hype, but this franchise completely defined my childhood. Getting The Master Chief Collection on Steam feels like repossessing my youth in the absolute best way possible. Having Reach, CE, Halo 2, Halo 3, ODST, and Halo 4 living together in one launcher is insane value.
Getting to replay these campaigns at an ultra-smooth frame rate feels incredible. Toggling between the classic 2004 graphics and the gorgeous Halo 2 Anniversary remakes gives me intense flashbacks to split-screen LAN parties with friends. The matchmaking mixer is perfect too. bouncing from a chaotic Big Team Battle in Halo 3 straight into a tight Slayer match on Reach never gets old.
If you want a flawless preservation of the absolute best era of gaming, this is it. 10/10. Wake up, Chief.

As an old school Bungie fan, I loved their Myth series.  It's the best RTS ever made, and easily one of my favorites.  Like fools, they abandoned the IP and instead focused on an FPS for consoles.  Now, almost a quarter of a century later I'm playing Halo.  Does it live up to the hype?

Halo: CE
Does not live up to the hype.  It's a good-ish game,  I like the music and the limit to two weapons.  The combat clicked for me once you get on a covenant ship, but (hot take alert) once the flood appears, the game's combat just gets boring.  So the parts that are good, it's basically Unreal with melee attacks, and boring vehicles.  Also, the maps are Oni-tier boring.  

Hopefully the other games get better, but regardless, I will at least get my money's worth.
